adjudicated.jp: 蝉がうるさい。
adjudicated.en: The cicadas are making loud,
adjudicated.assessment: The source simply says the cicadas are loud or noisy; 'making loud' is incomplete English.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'The cicadas are loud' or 'The cicadas are making a racket.'

adjudicated.jp: こんな暑いのに。
adjudicated.en: even when it's this hot.
adjudicated.assessment: The concessive fragment about the heat is preserved and joins the preceding line coherently.

adjudicated.jp: 奴らはいつだって本気だ。
adjudicated.en: Those guys are always serious.
adjudicated.assessment: The personified observation that they are always serious or giving it their all is conveyed.

adjudicated.jp: 「しかし」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Well then."
adjudicated.assessment: The conjunction marks contrast or reservation, whereas 'well then' advances to a conclusion or next action.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'Still,' 'But,' or another contrastive discourse marker.

adjudicated.jp: どうするかな、これから。
adjudicated.en: What do I do now.
adjudicated.assessment: The narrator's question about what to do next is accurately retained.

adjudicated.jp: 屋上が炎天下となると、涼める場所はさほどない。
adjudicated.en: With the rooftop under the blazing sun, that's not really a place to cool off in.
comments: The thing about Misato saying it's gonna get hot is a load; this isn't 9AM. She was just telling him that to send him away. There's no way Taichi is so damn dumb to believe her; this is a hint that the previous scene shouldn't gel with this, cicadas or not. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The source says that with the rooftop exposed to the blazing sun there are few places available to cool off; the rendering merely excludes the roof itself and omits the scarcity of alternatives.
adjudicated.remedy: Preserve the conclusion that few cooling-off places remain.

highlights.text: that's not really a place to cool off in

adjudicated.jp: 手近な教室をのぞいてみると、案の定授業中だった。
adjudicated.en: I tried peeking inside a class nearby, sure enough, a lesson was in progress.
adjudicated.assessment: The two independent clauses are joined only by a comma; the source relation is clear but the English sentence is mechanically defective.
adjudicated.remedy: Separate the clauses or join them with a conjunction or dash.

adjudicated.jp: 一年Ｅ組。
adjudicated.en: First Year, Class E.
comments: High School. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The class designation is accurate.

adjudicated.jp: まちこ先生が授業をしている。
adjudicated.en: The class is being taught by Machiko-sensei.
comments: http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miss_Machiko See CCA0022 for why this is 100% a reference. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The teacher and ongoing lesson are identified correctly.

adjudicated.jp: 佐藤真智子。
adjudicated.en: Satou Machiko.
comments: Curiously 佐藤真 Satou Makoto is a documentarist, nothing I can see, but 智子 Tomoko is a character in To Heart... nah, too random, it's obviously not it. There are some people with this name, but nothing obvious unfortunately; this will be so for most names. Either they're just red herrings or they're specific people I simply have no idea how to source. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The personal name is transcribed consistently.

adjudicated.jp: 教職二年目。
adjudicated.en: In her second year of teaching profession.
adjudicated.assessment: The fragment means that this is her second year as a teacher; the English omits the article and uses an unnatural construction.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'Her second year as a teacher.'

adjudicated.jp: 俺たちと同じ年度で教師になった。
adjudicated.en:
She had became teacher for the same class
year as us.
comments: It's actually uncertain if these two flow together, I suppose intentionally because "second year" could then easily misread as meaning Taichi is a second year, when he isn't in this flashback. The hint is above in how she teaches first years, although that may only be on this particular hour on this particular day. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The source says she became a teacher in the same academic year that the students began; it does not say she became a teacher for their class year, and the verb form is also wrong.
adjudicated.remedy: State the parallel timing of her starting as a teacher and their school year.

highlights.text:
became teacher for the same class
year as us

adjudicated.jp: 今ではすっかり女教師が板についている。
adjudicated.en:
Nowadays female teachers are something
pretty habitual,
comments: Begin Walls of Ambiguity! "Female teachers are normal these days" + "these days I'm used to female teachers so I don't molest them so much" -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The idiom says she has now thoroughly settled into or grown into the role of female teacher; the rendering generalizes to female teachers as a habitual phenomenon.
adjudicated.remedy: Keep her as the subject and render the idiom as being fully at home in the role.

highlights.text:
female teachers are something
pretty habitual

adjudicated.jp: だがまちこ先生は罪深い。
adjudicated.en: nevertheless, Machiko-sensei is sinful.
comments: More Misato parallels. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The mock-moralizing declaration is preserved.

adjudicated.jp: 罪っ子である。
adjudicated.en: Sinful to the core.
comments: Lit. "sinbaby", which sounds less silly in Japanese, but not entirely so. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The source coins a playful child-or-girl label from 'sin'; the rendering replaces that wordplay with an unsupported intensifier.
adjudicated.remedy: Recreate a compact playful label rather than escalating degree.

adjudicated.jp: その罪の多くは、シャツを内側から突き上げるふくらみに含まれていると言ってもいいだろう。
adjudicated.en:
It could probably be said that this wealth of
sins does include protrusions that force upwards
her shirt from the inside.
adjudicated.assessment: The image of the swelling that pushes up her shirt from within is recognizable, but the verb placement and plural abstraction are unidiomatic and obscure the mock claim that much of her sin resides there.
adjudicated.remedy: Make the swelling the clear object in which the sins reside and use natural English word order.

highlights.text:
does include protrusions that force upwards
her shirt

adjudicated.jp: 臀部はと言えばこれまた凶悪で、凶器となっている。
adjudicated.en:
And speaking of her buttocks, their sheer
infernal diabolicalness would make them
a dangerous weapon by themselves,
comments: Guess why I picked this reading... -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The exaggerated description of her buttocks as vicious enough to be a weapon is retained in a comparably heightened register.

adjudicated.jp: キレた１４歳の少年が手にするナイフと同じほどに危険だ。
adjudicated.en:
equally as dangerous as a knife in the
hands of a broken 14-year old boy.
comments: Except Taichi's between 15 and 16 by now, since he's 17 by the end of Summer next year (birthday would therefore be between this early Summer and September - wanna bet it's July 7?). So while it is a big hint in hindsight because this is Psychopath High, unless he got into school at that age i.e. he killed everyone at the Mansion not a year and a half before, which is impossible because he was at Gunjou at 13 for the Cultural Festival where he met Sakuraba, the true focus is the 7x2 in there. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The adjective describes a fourteen-year-old who has snapped or flown into a rage, not a boy who is broken.
adjudicated.remedy: Use an idiomatic phrase for an enraged or unhinged fourteen-year-old.

adjudicated.jp: と言わんばかりに張りつめるまろやかヒップ。
adjudicated.en:
Those round hips under the strain of having been
crammed tight into the Area of Youthful Male
Covetousness known as the depths of her Tight
Skirt seemed to say,
comments: Merged the line before and after the below. Couldn't make it work without losing too much steam otherwise. The Tight Skirt BGM title likely refers to this line. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: Despite absorbing adjacent setup into this segment, the rounded hips straining as though to speak are represented in the combined passage.

adjudicated.jp: 『こんな狭い場所じゃあちきの美肉はリラックスできないわよ！』
adjudicated.en:
『Aw, it's so tight here that this
beautiful flesh of mine just can't relax!』
comments: Origins of that あちき http://okwave.jp/qa/q6894804.html (J only). "I" that implies ex-prostitute, though it's sort of a cliche' in itself. This should sound at least sort-of vaguely off-ish, I guess. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The personified complaint about beautiful flesh being unable to relax in the cramped space is preserved.

adjudicated.jp: 尻の割れ目に横筋が橋を張るほどにぱっつんぱっつんなスカートの中央に、カッターで縦の切れ目をスーッと入れたいと思ったことは五度や十度じゃない。
adjudicated.en:
With a stritch and a stretch the cleft of the
ass created transversal stripes stretched like
bridges in the middle of her skirt that I thought
not five nor ten times to get a cutter and
caaarefully cut them transversally.
comments: That's the specific SFX adjective for when clothes are so tight that motion causes them to create that kind of ripple, here's a pic and description (in Japanese): http://dic.pixiv.net/a/%E3%81%B1%E3%81%A3%E3%81%A4%E3%82%93%E3%81%B1%E3%81%A3%E3%81%A4%E3%82%93 This should sound creepy on reread, like the knife above. It just means "several times", but let's consider it literally, as it is often a good thing to do with Tanaka: though technically it should mean more than ten times, if he didn't think five nor ten times then seven times would be an appropriate amount. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The source imagines making one vertical slit down the center of the tight skirt; the rendering changes both the direction and object to cutting plural stripes transversely.
adjudicated.remedy: Keep the horizontal bridging lines as description and the desired cut as a vertical slit in the skirt.

adjudicated.jp: 危険な女性だ。
adjudicated.en: She's a dangerous female.
adjudicated.assessment: The source calls her a dangerous woman; the nominal use of 'female' is needlessly clinical and unnatural in this narration.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'dangerous woman.'

adjudicated.jp: 悪の校長と番長らによって、妹（同校在籍の女生徒……明るく成績優秀でスポーツ万能で男女わけへだてなく人気があったりする）の弱みをネタに脅迫され性悦の極みに堕ちていきかねない。
adjudicated.en:
Because of a wicked headmaster and his gang of
ne'er-do-wells, her little sister (female student
enrolled in the same school... brilliant academic
results, excellent at sports and popular with
both genders without distinction) became her
weak point, so that this threatened sibling
may well be what casts her down into the extremes
of forced sexual ecstasy.
comments: The headmaster is sort of a character in here. I have no idea why or what, though. I suspect he used to be the villain in Taichi's Settei before Miki came in. ...I'm not actually sure who is Imouto here. I wonder if it means Taichi himself in his gender confusion, though in that case she reads like Youko, which gets a big hmmm. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The woman is blackmailed by villains who exploit leverage involving her younger sister and may thereby be driven into sexual degradation; the rendering makes the threatened sister the agent that casts her down.
adjudicated.remedy: Keep the villains as agents of the blackmail and the sister as the leverage used against the woman.

highlights.text:
this threatened sibling
may well be what casts her down

adjudicated.jp: そんな仏国書院的な危機から、俺はいつでも彼女を守りたいのである。
adjudicated.en:
I desire to protect her from that danger worthy
of a certain French publishing house forever and
always.
comments: http://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E3%83%95%E3%83%A9%E3%83%B3%E3%82%B9%E6%9B%B8%E9%99%A2 it's actually written in katakana, not kanji like here. Curiously, the avid reader of that kind of romance novels would be Yusa, wouldn't she. Is she imouto then? Who is Imouto? I knew I should've watched that instead of Da Capo III... -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The publishing-house allusion and exaggerated protective declaration are both retained, if indirectly.

adjudicated.jp: 一年生の時、副担任になったまちこ先生に飽くなきセクハラを繰り返し、ついには授業中に泣かせてしまったうえ三日間無断欠勤をさせてしまったことが、未だに悔やまれる。
adjudicated.en:
As a first year student, Machiko-sensei became
our substitute homeroom teacher, and I repeatedly
and insatiably harassed her until eventually I
made her break down in tears in the middle of
class and take a three day leave from work
without permission, an event I still regret.
comments: It's around as forced as it is in the original, but that "as a first year student" is intended to recapture that said time hasn't necessarily ended. Whether he regrets his pranks or her reaction is intentionally unclear. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The title is assistant or deputy homeroom teacher, not a substitute temporarily replacing another teacher.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'assistant homeroom teacher' or the locally established equivalent.

adjudicated.jp: ……そして俺は停学を食らって、先輩に「停学君」とからかわれるようになった。
adjudicated.en:
...and then I was struck with suspension, and
Senpai began teasing me as "Suspension-kun".
comments: see CCA0002, CCC4006 and more. Uncertain if this is before or after her nickname for him. That students at Evil High would be given leaves of absence for their behavior is just stupid beyond comprehension. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The narrator was suspended or got slapped with a suspension; 'was struck with suspension' is not idiomatic English.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'I got suspended' or an equivalently forceful idiom.

adjudicated.jp: ま、それで親しくなったからいいんだけど。
adjudicated.en: Well, we got closer because of that, so it's good.
adjudicated.assessment: The retrospective consolation that it brought them closer is preserved.

adjudicated.jp: さておき。
adjudicated.en: Anyway.
adjudicated.assessment: The discourse pivot is rendered accurately.

adjudicated.jp: 以来、まちこ先生と俺との接点は消滅した。
adjudicated.en:
Ever since, the points of contact between me
and Machiko-sensei have vanished.
comments: It reads sarcastically like "times at which I could grope her", but taken literally it's thematically important. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The source says their opportunities for contact disappeared; the plural technical phrase is a stiff calque that makes the relationship sound geometric.
adjudicated.remedy: Say that he had no further contact with her.

highlights.text:
points of contact between me
and Machiko-sensei

adjudicated.jp: 二年を待たずして副担が変わり、受け持ち授業からもいなくなった。
adjudicated.en:
Without waiting for second year the substitute
changed, and she was no more even in the class
she was in charge of.
comments: But did the teacher change, or did she stop existing to Taichi due to what is possibly still a trauma for him? -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: Before his second year, the assistant homeroom assignment changed and she also ceased teaching any of his classes. The rendering again calls her a substitute and does not express whose timetable lost her.
adjudicated.remedy: State both the changed assistant-homeroom assignment and her disappearance from the narrator's classes.

highlights.text:
the substitute
changed, and she was no more even in the class
she was in charge of

adjudicated.jp: さらば青い思い出。
adjudicated.en: Fare thee well, memories of the green.
comments: See CCC3004, CCD2002 -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The color adjective evokes youth or immaturity here; literal 'memories of the green' is not a functioning English expression.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'youthful memories' or recreate the color metaphor idiomatically.

adjudicated.jp: セクハラ、ほどほどにしておけばよかったな。
adjudicated.en:
I just wish I had the kept sexual harassment
within moderation.
adjudicated.assessment: The intended regret about keeping the harassment within bounds is recognizable, but the English contains a basic word-order and article error.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'I wish I'd kept the sexual harassment within reason.'

adjudicated.jp: でもどうせ嫌われるならもっと揉んでおけばよかった、と考えてる時点で俺はもう終わってるんだろう人として。
adjudicated.en:
But if being hated was the result no matter what,
then I wish I had given a further once-over to
all that, though having those thoughts at this
point means that I'm all but done as a person.
comments: "I wish I had rubbed more" + "I wish I had worried about that more". 揉 will often be used in both its meanings many many times. Say Without Saying, once again. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The explicit counter-regret is that he should have groped or fondled more; the vague phrase removes the concrete act that makes his self-condemnation land.
adjudicated.remedy: Name the groping directly enough to preserve the joke and moral self-indictment.

highlights.text:
given a further once-over to
all that

adjudicated.jp: 「ふー」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Sigh..."
adjudicated.assessment: The exhaled sigh is conveyed adequately.

adjudicated.jp: とにかく、このまま廊下をウロウロしてたら誰かに見つかる。
adjudicated.en: Anyway, if I keep loitering in the corridors like this someone'll find me.
adjudicated.assessment: The risk of being found while continuing to loiter in the corridor is accurate.

adjudicated.jp: 食券を買ってから部室に行こう。
adjudicated.en: Let's go to the club room after buying a meal ticket.
adjudicated.assessment: The internal plan to buy a meal ticket before going to the clubroom is preserved.

adjudicated.jp: 完璧計画爆誕。
adjudicated.en: The explosive birth of a perfect project.
comments: See CCA0006. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: Explosive birth preserves 爆誕, and project is a defensible contextual rendering of 計画. The immediate scheme remains recognizable, so no confirmed source error is established.
adjudicated.remedy: Optional idiomatic revision; no confirmed source-bound correction is established.

adjudicated.jp: Ａ定食は三時間目には売り切れるから、確実に食べたい時は一時間目の終わりと同時に食堂に赴くことになる。
adjudicated.en: Meal set A is usually sold out by third period, so if one wants to eat it with certainty they have to be heading towards the cafeteria as soon as first period is over.
adjudicated.assessment: The sellout timing and need to go at the end of first period are conveyed accurately.

adjudicated.jp: それでも多少、行列はできる。
adjudicated.en: Even then, there's a bit of a line,
adjudicated.assessment: The continuing presence of a modest line is accurately conveyed as part of the sentence spanning the next unit.

adjudicated.jp: 二時間目に遅刻してしまうこともあるわけだ。
adjudicated.en: therefore some will come back late for second period at times.
adjudicated.assessment: The consequence that people can return late for second period is preserved.

adjudicated.jp: こういうことが多発すると、たまに思い出したように『食券事前買い禁止令』が公布されたりする。
adjudicated.en: If this happens frequently enough, occasionally they seem to remember to make the official promulgation of the Prohibition of Meal Ticket Pre-Sale.
adjudicated.assessment: The deliberately official register of the periodically remembered advance-purchase ban is retained.

adjudicated.jp: 数をもっと多く用意してくれればいいのに。
adjudicated.en: But it'd be better if they just made more of them.
adjudicated.assessment: The wish that the cafeteria would prepare more portions is conveyed.

adjudicated.jp: 誰もがそう思う。
adjudicated.en: Everybody thinks that.
adjudicated.assessment: The universal agreement is exact.

adjudicated.jp: だが無駄をはぶくためか、定食は数量限定が鉄の掟。
adjudicated.en: However, to cut back on waste or something, the set meal being available in limited number is an iron rule.
comments: The supply will not change in response to changes in demand. This is a strongly capitalist critique of this kind of behavior by state-run institutions, well in line with Tanaka's masked but fundamentally subversive and ultimately culturally anti-Japanese attitude. Just wait until below! -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The limited-quantity rule is semantically present, but this count construction is not grammatical English.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'available only in limited quantities.'

adjudicated.jp: だからこんな機会を逃す手はない。
adjudicated.en: Therefore, there's no way I'm missing this opportunity.
adjudicated.assessment: The determination not to miss the opportunity is accurately retained.

adjudicated.jp: さすがに一限目の途中なら行列もないしな。
adjudicated.en: As it's midway through first period there shouldn't be a line.
adjudicated.assessment: The expectation that there will be no line during first period is conveyed.

adjudicated.jp: がらすきだった。
adjudicated.en: It was almost entirely uninhabited.
comments: "Garasuki". It will be one of the descriptions of the Cross World. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The place is almost empty or sparsely occupied, not literally without inhabitants or residents.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'almost empty.'

adjudicated.jp: 「おばちゃん、エース定食」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Madam, set meal Ace."
comments: Unknown if this is Yusa's mom... -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The address is a casual call to the cafeteria lady, and the named meal modifies the set-meal noun; the English is overly formal and reverses the name order.
adjudicated.remedy: Use a casual 'ma'am' or equivalent followed by 'the Ace set meal.'

adjudicated.jp: 無事に食券を買えた。
adjudicated.en: I was able to buy my meal ticket without problems.
comments: ...but I suspect it is, with the actual chat being snip'd. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The successful purchase without incident is accurately conveyed.

adjudicated.jp: らくちんらくちん。
adjudicated.en: Easy life mine, just an easy life.
comments: Hum, see CCA0013. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The repeated playful adjective means that the task was easy or easy-peasy; the rendering invents an ungrammatical claim about an easy life.
adjudicated.remedy: Use a light repeated expression such as 'Easy, easy.'

highlights.text: Easy life mine, just an easy life

adjudicated.jp: 部室に入ると、パイプ椅子に座って雑誌を読んでいた男が顔をあげた。
adjudicated.en: On entering the club room, a male who was sitting on a folding chair and reading a magazine raised his head.
comments: See CCD1001: he calls women a fairly creepy "females" back then, and see below. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The source refers to a man; nominal 'a male' is clinical and unnatural for ordinary narrative identification.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'a man.'

adjudicated.jp: 「いやいやいや、友貴先生じゃないですか」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Well well well, if it isn't Tomoki-sensei."
adjudicated.assessment: The mock-surprised greeting and joking form of address are preserved.

adjudicated.jp: 「こんなところで奇遇ですな。先生もアレですか？　こっちの方もいける口で？」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "What a coincidence finding you here. Are you doing 'that' as well, Sensei? You will offer me something to wet my lips as well?"
comments: Drinking. This is clearer with the thing below about the milk carton. Curiously the expression seems to be tied to alcohol drinking, perhaps since CCZRooftop was cut it lost this connection? -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: Together with the raised-pinky gesture, the speaker is insinuating that the other man is also interested in that sort of partner or pursuit. The rendering instead asks to be offered a drink, eliminating the insinuation and gesture-dependent joke.
adjudicated.remedy: Use an indirect but intelligible question that connects the pinky gesture to being interested in women.

highlights.text: You will offer me something to wet my lips as well

adjudicated.jp: 小指を立てる。
adjudicated.en: I raise a pinky.
comments: Means girl/girlfriend. Tomoki has a GF and Taichi's jealous, see below. Odd he'd do it here, though see CCD3003 when Miki does it. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The physical gesture of raising a pinky is accurately retained.

adjudicated.en: Tomoki: "Well..."
adjudicated.assessment: The hesitant response is conveyed.

adjudicated.jp: 冴えない顔でそう応じる。
adjudicated.en: He answers with a sullen face.
comments: Tsukkomi fail. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The expression is dull, listless, or unenthused; 'sullen' adds resentment or petulance not present in the source.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'with an unenthusiastic expression' or equivalent.

adjudicated.jp: 友貴は防御時のアドリブが全然きかないタイプだ。
adjudicated.en: Tomoki's the type that just can't ad-lib an effective counter on time.
adjudicated.assessment: The characterization that he cannot improvise an effective defense or retort is substantively preserved.

adjudicated.jp: コンパでは善人だが退屈な男と分類されるに違いない。
adjudicated.en: At a social mixer he'd be categorized as the nice but boring guy, no mistake.
adjudicated.assessment: The imagined social-mixer classification as nice but boring is accurate.

adjudicated.jp: 「さぼりか？　さぼりなのか？」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Cutting? Cutting aren't you?"
adjudicated.assessment: The repeated accusation is that he is skipping class. The bare verb 'cutting' does not carry that sense here, and the tag-like repetition is ungrammatical.
adjudicated.remedy: Use an idiomatic repeated accusation such as 'Skipping class? You are, aren't you?'

adjudicated.jp: 「そっちこそ」
adjudicated.en: Tomoki: "You too."
adjudicated.assessment: The reciprocal retort is conveyed accurately.

adjudicated.jp: 「うちのクラスは自習になったんだ」
adjudicated.en: Tomoki: "Our class became self-study, 's all."
comments: See CCA0022. Is that just a free period? -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The class was assigned a self-study period; a class cannot idiomatically 'become self-study.'
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'Our class has a self-study period.'

adjudicated.jp: 再び雑誌に目を戻し、パックのコーヒー牛乳をすすった。
adjudicated.en: Returning his eyes to the magazine once again, he sipped coffee milk from a carton.
adjudicated.assessment: Returning his gaze to the magazine and sipping carton coffee milk are both retained.

adjudicated.jp: なるほど。
adjudicated.en: I see.
adjudicated.assessment: The brief realization is exact.

adjudicated.jp: それで抜け出して、ここでくつろいでるわけだ。
adjudicated.en: He slipped out of that, then he came here to relax a bit.
adjudicated.assessment: The inference that he slipped away and is relaxing there is accurately conveyed.

adjudicated.jp: いいひと属性のくせしてワルぶりやがって。
adjudicated.en: That damnable vice of people with the Nice Guy Attribute of acting worse than they are.
comments: "Attribute" will recur. This is specifically discussing his character archetype. Sooo very telling of Taichi more than Tomoki, isn't he? See below. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The narrator mocks this particular nice guy for putting on a bad-boy act. The rendering turns it into a generalized vice shared by a category of people and weakens the direct sneer.
adjudicated.remedy: Keep the individual as subject: despite his nice-guy trait, he is trying to act bad.

highlights.text: vice of people with the Nice Guy Attribute of acting worse than they are

adjudicated.jp: 「食券は？」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Meal ticket?"
adjudicated.assessment: The clipped question about the meal ticket is preserved.

adjudicated.jp: 「買ったよ」
adjudicated.en: Tomoki: "Bought it."
adjudicated.assessment: The concise confirmation is accurate.

adjudicated.jp: 「やるな」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Not bad."
adjudicated.assessment: The approving 'not bad' response is appropriate.

adjudicated.en: Tomoki: "..."
adjudicated.assessment: The silent response is preserved; local canonical order uniquely selects this duplicate occurrence.

adjudicated.jp: シカトかい。
adjudicated.en: Ostracism?
comments: Ignoring him, but not the same way Touko does. シカト会 is more of an obvious misreading than an alternate one to 'is he giving me a cold shoulder?', but it's so awesome I was tempted to use it until practically the final moment. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The slang complaint means that he is being ignored or given the silent treatment, not socially ostracized.
adjudicated.remedy: Use a colloquial complaint such as 'Ignoring me, huh?'

adjudicated.jp: なんか気が抜けた。
adjudicated.en: That sends me down a bit.
adjudicated.assessment: The narrator feels deflated or has the wind taken out of him; 'sends me down' is vague and non-idiomatic.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'That kind of deflated me.'

adjudicated.jp: どだい放送部はキャラ的分業化が進んでいて、ツッコミ担当の友貴に悪ノリは期待できない。
adjudicated.en: The division of characterizational labor in the Broadcast Club is basically voluntary, so it can't be expected for Tomoki to get carried away when he's in charge of the Straight-Man role.
comments: Ah, these are the design docs that Tanaka interwove throughout the story. This would mean "I didn't have specific character roles in mind when designing the Club", see CCA0030. I don't think you can use "characterizational", but "division of labor" just demands that form. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The source says the club's division of character roles is already highly developed. It says nothing about the arrangement being voluntary; that invention disrupts the reason a designated straight man cannot be expected to join the escalation.
adjudicated.remedy: State that the role-based division of labor is firmly established.

adjudicated.jp: 窓から外を見る。
adjudicated.en: I looked outside from the window.
adjudicated.assessment: This immediate narrative action is in the present tense, while the rendering shifts it into the past amid surrounding present-tense narration.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'I look outside through the window.'

adjudicated.jp: 強い日差し。
adjudicated.en: Strong sunshine.
adjudicated.assessment: The fragment describing intense sunlight is retained.

adjudicated.jp: 「暑いな、今日も」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Another hot day today, innit."
adjudicated.assessment: The source is casual but does not motivate a conspicuously British dialect tag, which imposes an unrelated regional voice.
adjudicated.remedy: Use a neutral casual tag or omit it.

adjudicated.jp: 「冷蔵庫にもう一個あるけど」
adjudicated.en: Tomoki: "There's still one left in the fridge tho."
comments: This connects to above. He thinks Taichi's just being annoying because he wants a drink. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The information that one more remains in the refrigerator is preserved.

adjudicated.jp: 「８０円だっけ？」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "80 yen was it?"
comments: Number eight... -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The uncertain recollection of the price is accurate.

adjudicated.jp: 「そー」
adjudicated.en: Tomoki: "Yep."
adjudicated.assessment: The drawn-out casual affirmation is represented adequately.

adjudicated.jp: 「もらうわ」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "I shall be taking it, yes."
comments: Girly. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The source is a casual 'I'll take it'; the rendering imposes conspicuous formality and adds a mannered final affirmation.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'I'll take it.'

highlights.text: I shall be taking it, yes

adjudicated.jp: 突き出た手に小銭を落として、備え付けの冷蔵庫を開ける。
adjudicated.en: I drop coins into the proffered hand, and opened the provisions refrigerator.
adjudicated.assessment: The coordinated present-tense actions are split across present and past, and the installed or provided refrigerator becomes a nonsensical 'provisions refrigerator.'
adjudicated.remedy: Keep both verbs in the same tense and describe the built-in or provided refrigerator.

highlights.text: drop coins into the proffered hand, and opened the provisions refrigerator

adjudicated.jp: 「……あの、全部の硬貨に正倉院が刻まれているんですけど？」
adjudicated.en: Tomoki: "...uhm, but every coin here has the Shoushou-in engraved on it instead of the Byoudou-in...?"
comments: ...and the number eight is false. Can't find any coin that actually does, probably just a horrid pun. Adapted to fit. See CCC3012B, CCC3019B. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The wrong-building coin joke is preserved, and naming the expected building supplies the cultural contrast without changing its function.

adjudicated.jp: クレームは無視して、パックをすすった。
adjudicated.en: Ignoring the objection, I sucked on the carton.
adjudicated.assessment: He sips the drink from its carton; the rendering makes the carton itself the object being sucked and sounds physically different.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'I sipped from the carton.'

adjudicated.jp: 「もう」
adjudicated.en: Tomoki: "Aww."
comments: Betrayed, and his reaction is... nothing. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The short exasperated complaint is conveyed.

adjudicated.jp: それ以上の追求はなく、気怠い時間が流れた。
adjudicated.en: With no further pursuit of the matter, listlessly the time flowed on.
adjudicated.assessment: The source describes a languid stretch of time passing; the adverb is mechanically attached to time as though time itself behaved listlessly.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'a languid silence settled in' or 'time passed languidly.'

adjudicated.jp: 窓際にずらりと並ぶ、様々なモニターと機材を乗せた長テーブルを見やる。
adjudicated.en: My gaze turns to the several monitors, lined up in a row together with other equipment, arranged on the long table by the window.
comments: As mentioned, it's literal monitors here, not transceivers, making this line be somewhat nonsensical. I wouldn't consider a cassette stereo, randomly tossed together speakers, a boom box and what seems to be a line of old Macintoshes(?) as "broadcast club equipment". Unless that's intentional, this BG is fairly thorough design fail. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The gaze, window-side long table, row of monitors, and other equipment are all retained.

adjudicated.jp: 放送部の機材だ。
adjudicated.en: It's the equipment of the Broadcast Club.
adjudicated.assessment: The equipment is correctly identified as belonging to the club.

adjudicated.jp: すぐ隣が、放送室となっている。
adjudicated.en: Immediately next door is the Broadcast Room itself.
adjudicated.assessment: The adjacent broadcast room is accurately located.

adjudicated.jp: こっちは待機室で、たまり場だ。
adjudicated.en: This is the ready room, so it's a gathering area.
comments: The point is the division between the two. This is the side seen; like the city beyond the mountains, what's on the Other Side is of no consequence. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The current room's dual function as waiting room and hangout is conveyed.

adjudicated.jp: 電源があるのをいいことに、小型冷蔵庫を置いたりゲーム機を常備したり携帯充電器が一列に並んでいたりと校内でも屈指の無法空間となっている。
adjudicated.en: It's nice that there's electricity, so there's a small refrigerator, game consoles on reserve, and cellphone chargers lined up in a row, making this into the foremost lawless space inside the school.
comments: And no one goes inside to see all this stuff. Don't clubs have supervising teachers? Compare Mammoth below. Rules in this school are applied with the same zeal as Misato does. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The occupants take advantage of having electrical power as license to install appliances and chargers. The rendering turns that causal criticism into a generic statement that electricity is nice.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'Taking full advantage of the power outlets...' or equivalent.

adjudicated.jp: 「あれ、機材の配線外れてない？」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "My, isn't the wiring of the machine disconnected?"
comments: Specifying wiring as that's what Tomoki's good at when it comes to the antenna, also see CCX0001. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The source refers to the equipment's wiring generally, not the wiring of a single machine.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'Isn't the equipment disconnected?' or 'Haven't the cables been unplugged?'

adjudicated.jp: 「新しいマシン組むから、ちょっと構成変える」
adjudicated.en: Tomoki: "I'm putting together a new machine, so I'm changing stuff around a bit."
comments: He's assembling a new PC, though it actually isn't said that it's a PC, the term is the generic one for "antenna equipment". This is quite odd. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: Building a new machine and rearranging the setup are conveyed naturally.

adjudicated.jp: 「ふーん」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Uh-huh."
adjudicated.assessment: The noncommittal acknowledgment is appropriate.

adjudicated.jp: 友貴はこれでけっこうなパソコン少年で、美希とよくＣＰＵだのメモリだのの会話に花を咲かせている。
adjudicated.en: Tomoki here is quite the PC guy, and a lot of conversations bloom between him and Miki about CPU and RAM and those things.
comments: Her archetype isn't as visible as, say, Touko's, but Miki is intended to be a Genius Loli. In reality, I doubt Miki and Tomoki exchange as much as five words throughout the story. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: His computer enthusiasm and frequent lively technical conversations are substantively preserved.

adjudicated.jp: 別の学校に通う一個下の可愛い彼女がいて、出会いはＢＢＳだそうだ。
adjudicated.en: He has a cute girlfriend from another school one year younger than him that he seems to have met on a BBS.
comments: Should be an Internet forum, not a literal BBS. Not that the two aren't called the same in Japan. "From another school" means she's a Normie, but apparently from the same town. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The girlfriend's age, different school, and reported BBS meeting are retained.

adjudicated.jp: 友貴が入院している頃、一度本人と出会ったことがある。
adjudicated.en: I once met her myself when Tomoki was hospitalized.
comments: When Misato cut his tendons, meaning the event dates to when Taichi and Tomoki knew each other, meaning no more than a year before. Likely it wasn't weeks before, as well, as in CCD1001 he says the event was a year before i.e. now. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The narrator's one meeting with her during the hospitalization is accurate.

adjudicated.jp: 見舞いに行ったときだ。
adjudicated.en: She came during visiting hours.
adjudicated.assessment: The narrator met her when he went to visit the hospitalized friend. The rendering reverses the visitor and invents a reference to visiting hours.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'It was when I went to visit him.'

adjudicated.jp: 『あっ、あの、と、とと友貴くんがお世話になってますっっっ』
adjudicated.en: Girlfriend: 『Ah, uhm, tha-, tha-tha-thank you for taking care of Tomoki-kun...!』
comments: Generally, lines by unvoiced characters outside of Taichi gets paraphrased - Touko's maid in the finale, the Tasaki owner - but not this one for unknown reasons. See CCE0001 for the only other mention of this girl. Although never really mentioned, she sounds like she's basically Yusa. Which is basically Misato. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The flustered thanks and stammer are recreated effectively.

adjudicated.jp: と頭をさげてきた制服の着こなしからして一味違う激キュートな生命体の出現に、ショックを受けた俺の記憶は未だおぼろげだ。
adjudicated.en: And she bowed her head, that Ultra Kyute life form so unique just in the elegant way she wore her uniform, that my memories are still vague from the shock of meeting her.
comments: He's using life-form just like with Machiko. See CCD1001 and above: beats the utterly contemptuous "female", so that's why I used the equivalent 'male' above. Also see CCD0002: he didn't always treat Tomoki with even this little respect, either. The vagueness of memories is the same as CCA0001, so his memories vaguefy from shock as well. MEMORY HUNTER!!! -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The deliberately misspelled English coinage is unexplained and the surrounding sentence attaches multiple 'that' clauses without a stable structure, blunting the claim that even her uniform styling marked an exceptionally cute life-form.
adjudicated.remedy: Use a readable comic superlative and rebuild the sentence around the narrator's shock-blurred memory.

adjudicated.jp: きっと友貴が求めれば、脱ぎたての下着だってくれるに違いなかった。
adjudicated.en: Make no mistake, if Tomoki were just to ask, she'd strip off and hand over her panties.
comments: See CCA0030. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The exaggerated certainty that she would hand over freshly removed underwear if asked is functionally preserved.
The extended silent pause is retained.

adjudicated.jp: 「いてっ！　なにすんの！？」
adjudicated.en: Tomoki: "OW-! Whassat for?!"
adjudicated.assessment: The pained protest is idiomatic and forceful.

adjudicated.jp: 「急に悔しくなって……」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "I felt annoyed all of a sudden..."
comments: ...but is it because Tomoki has a girlfriend, or is this about Youko? -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The sudden resentful or frustrated feeling is conveyed closely enough.

adjudicated.jp: 「はい、なにが？　わけわかんざき」
adjudicated.en: Tomoki: "Huh, with what? I don't get a watch of whatcha sayin'."
comments: Just a hideous pun. Dumped something appropriately crappy in there, since that's the point. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: Watch of whatcha sayin’ is an intentionally terrible replacement pun, and the very next line explicitly judges the character’s jokes as painfully unfunny. The target joke therefore performs the same social and comic function even though its lexical material changes.
adjudicated.remedy: Recreate the sentence-ending name pun with an intelligible English setup or retain the meaning and flag the wordplay.

adjudicated.jp: 友貴はギャグも最高につまらない。
adjudicated.en: Even Tomoki's gags are the height of boring.
adjudicated.assessment: The judgment that his jokes are supremely boring is retained.

adjudicated.jp: こんなヤツにあんな可愛いガー（ＧＩＲＬ）がひっつくなんて、間違ってる。不潔。
adjudicated.en: It's just wrong for that cute GRRR(l) to stick to this guy. It's filthy.
comments: http://thejadednetwork.com/sfx/search/?keyword=%E3%82%AC%E3%83%BC&submitSearch=Search+SFX&x= hmmm, going with grrr+girl. The comparisons with Youko continue, see CCA0027. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The stylized English interruption around 'girl' is creatively recast while the jealous judgment remains intact.

adjudicated.en: Girl: "...heheh!"
adjudicated.assessment: The source is a wordless caught-breath or suppressed reaction; explicit laughter is added without support and changes the emotional signal.
adjudicated.remedy: Use a breath, catch, or nonverbal ellipsis without specifying laughter.

adjudicated.jp: くすくす笑いが聞こえた。
adjudicated.en: I could hear a giggly laugh.
adjudicated.assessment: The audible quiet giggle is conveyed.

adjudicated.jp: 「あれえ、いたんだ？」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Myyy, she was here?"
adjudicated.assessment: The speaker addresses the newly noticed girl directly: 'Oh, you were here?' The rendering changes the addressee into a third-person subject.
adjudicated.remedy: Use second person.

adjudicated.jp: 放送室から来たんだろう、眼鏡をかけた小柄な少女がいた。
adjudicated.en: A bespectacled girl of small build was there, likely having come out of the broadcast room.
comments: What was someone with a pathological fear of solitude doing alone in the broadcast room? When Tomoki was here? The answer is simple, if we go by what Taichi does usually: fantasizing and flashbacking. And she came there without him noticing. And wait just a little! -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The small bespectacled girl and her probable route from the broadcast room are accurately presented.

adjudicated.jp: 「あいかわらず先輩がたは……」
adjudicated.en: Girl: "Always like this, you two Senpai..."
adjudicated.assessment: Her weary comment about the two upperclassmen being unchanged is substantively retained.

adjudicated.jp: 「がたって」
adjudicated.en: Tomoki: "'You two'..."
comments: Sounds ugly, but -gata is too uncommon to leave and it's used like twice. Regrettably adapted. Payoff in CCB0006. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The response isolates and reacts to the pluralizing form of address through an intelligible English paraphrase.

adjudicated.jp: 後輩の福原みゆきだった。
adjudicated.en: She was Fukuhara Miyuki, a Kouhai of mine.
comments: Same Hara as Touko's last name. Fuku here is "fortune". -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The junior student is identified accurately by name and relationship.

adjudicated.jp: 「おっす。元気？」
adjudicated.en: Tomoki: "Hail. In spirits?"
adjudicated.assessment: The source is an ordinary casual greeting and check-in; the English sounds archaic and omits the grammar needed for a question about wellbeing.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'Hey. How are you?'

adjudicated.jp: 「おやあ？　おやおやぁ？」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Ohhh? Oh-my-myyy?"
adjudicated.assessment: The exaggerated intrigued reaction is recreated effectively.

adjudicated.jp: 「な、なんです？」
adjudicated.en: Miyuki: "Wh-, what is it?"
adjudicated.assessment: The wary stammered question is accurate.

adjudicated.jp: 警戒してのけぞるみゆき。
adjudicated.en: Miyuki leans back guardedly.
adjudicated.assessment: Her guarded backward lean is conveyed.

adjudicated.jp: 「なんて地味っ娘なんだ」
adjudicated.en:
Miyuki: "You're still gonna call me plain again are you?"
Taichi: "Why you so plain, why!"
comments: This sounds like there's a line feed missing, and indeed it's so in the console version, but the two saying this simultaneously is just so much funnier, so I didn't fix this one bug. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The source contains only the narrator's exclamation that she is an extraordinarily plain girl. A full anticipatory response by the girl is invented, and the remaining English line is itself malformed.
adjudicated.remedy: Remove the invented reply and render the single exclamation idiomatically.

highlights.text: Miyuki: "You're still gonna call me plain again are you?"

adjudicated.jp: 「あああああ……」
adjudicated.en: Miyuki: "Awwww..."
comments: あx5, but see below... -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The drawn-out distressed vocalization is reasonably represented.

adjudicated.jp: 少女はがくがくと震えた。
adjudicated.en: The girl shook with a clattering.
comments: ...what's she even so nervous for? -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The girl trembles violently; 'with a clattering' treats the mimetic manner as an unexplained accompanying object and suggests hard objects striking.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'The girl shook violently.'

adjudicated.jp: 「うーん、君はなー、どーしてこう地味なのかなー。どーして君の髪どめのゴムはすごく安そうなの？　どうして眉がこんなにぽわぽわしてるの？　どうしてスカートもっと短くしないの？」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Yeaaah... whyyy you... whyyy you even so plain! Whyyy does the rubber of your hair bands look so cheap, hm? Why are your eyebrows all thin and faint like this? Why isn't this skirt just a little bit shorter?"
comments: Mugi (K-On!)'s the only character I found defined has having "powa-powa" eyebrows, but they don't fit Miyuki's pic now that she has one. It's not visible in these dolls, but in the 360 data files there's a set that's cut below the knee, and her skirt is the longest of all skirted characters except maybe Touko. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The eyebrows are described with a soft, fluffy, or fuzzy mimetic quality, not as thin and faint; the insult's concrete visual target changes.
adjudicated.remedy: Use an idiomatic description of fluffy or fuzzy eyebrows.

adjudicated.jp: 「きゃあ、スカートはちょっとっ」
adjudicated.en: Miyuki: "Kyah! The skirt, really now..."
adjudicated.assessment: The startled objection involving the skirt is retained.

adjudicated.jp: 「うーん」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Yeeeah."
adjudicated.assessment: The drawn-out considering sound is preserved.

adjudicated.jp: 「首筋を優しく撫でないでくださいよっ、きゃっ、耳に指入れないでぇっ！？」
adjudicated.en: Miyuki: "Please don't gently stroke the back of my neck! KYAH! Don't put your fingers inside my eaaar!"
comments: See CCZDXC. Mi(yu)ki. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: Both physical protests and their escalating panic are accurately conveyed.

adjudicated.jp: 愛撫攻撃。
adjudicated.en: Attack of caresses.
adjudicated.assessment: The mock attack label is preserved.

adjudicated.jp: 「もとはいいのにねぇ」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "So the outside is fine theeen!"
adjudicated.assessment: The phrase says her underlying material or natural looks are good despite her plain styling; it does not contrast an exterior with an interior.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'You've got good raw material' or a natural equivalent.

adjudicated.en: Miyuki: "Huh...?"
adjudicated.assessment: The confused response is exact.

adjudicated.jp: 「もったいない、もったいない」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Wasteful, so wasteful!"
adjudicated.assessment: The exclamation means 'what a waste' repeated, not that the girl is wasteful as an adjective.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'What a waste, what a waste.'

adjudicated.jp: 「もったいないから食ーべちゃおっと」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "So wasteful I wanna eat it aaall!"
comments: See CCD0021. Who was it at fault? -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: Because letting her go to waste would be a shame, the speaker playfully decides to eat her up. The rendering uses an impersonal object and adds total consumption rather than directing the tease at the girl.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'What a waste—maybe I'll just eat you up.'

adjudicated.en: Miyuki: "Huh?"
adjudicated.assessment: The baffled reaction is accurately preserved.

adjudicated.jp: かぷりこ
adjudicated.en: Caplico!
comments: WOOOAAAAH they like exist in the west and all??? I think this is a sound effect. Food isn't normally sound effects, but in Japan it's known to happen, about as frequently as random outbreaks of gender-bending. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The candy-brand-like chomp pun is retained through the product name.

adjudicated.jp: 身をかがめて、耳にかぶりついたのでした。
adjudicated.en: I bent over her and bit into her ears.
adjudicated.assessment: The action is biting into one ear; pluralizing it changes the physical image.
adjudicated.remedy: Use singular 'ear.'

adjudicated.jp: 女の子の香りがしました。
adjudicated.en: There it was, the smell of young girl.
comments: See Youko now. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The source says she smelled like a girl. The English omits the needed article or possessive construction and adds a youth qualifier not present in the line.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'She smelled like a girl' or 'I caught a girl's scent.'

adjudicated.jp: 童話調に言っても、セクハラには違いないが。
adjudicated.en: I may say this in the tone of a fairy-tale, but make no mistake, this is sexual harassment.
adjudicated.assessment: The contrast between fairy-tale narration and the unchanged fact of harassment is preserved.

adjudicated.jp: 「あわああああああああっ！！？？」
adjudicated.en: Miyuki: "AwAaAaAaAaA!!!???"
comments: あx8 in that second part... but WAIT! There were x5 above, weren't there? Now add the first A and the A in the 'wah'. That's 7! -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The panicked extended cry is recreated with equivalent force.

adjudicated.jp: みゆきがエクスタシーに達した（嘘）。
adjudicated.en: Miyuki peaked into ecstasy (lies).
adjudicated.assessment: The mock narration says she reached ecstasy, followed by a singular admission that this is a lie. 'Peaked into' is not idiomatic and plural 'lies' changes the aside.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'Miyuki reached ecstasy. (Lie.)'

adjudicated.jp: 「……やめてあげなよ、そこのいじめっ子」
adjudicated.en: Tomoki: "...just stop that already, you damn bully."
adjudicated.assessment: The intervention telling the bully to stop is retained, with slightly stronger casual emphasis.

adjudicated.jp: 「お、なんだなんだ、彼女がいるくせにさらにロックオンか？」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Oh, lookie lookie, you got a girlfriend damn you but you're engaging in further Lock-On?"
adjudicated.assessment: The accusation that he is locking on to another target despite already having a girlfriend is recoverable, but the gerund construction is not grammatical natural dialogue.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'you're locking on to someone else too?'

adjudicated.jp: 「か、関係ないだろー！」
adjudicated.en: Tomoki: "Th-, that's got nothing to do with this!"
adjudicated.assessment: The stammered defensive rejection is accurately conveyed.

adjudicated.jp: 「このラブラチオ・スナイパーが」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Why, you Lovellatio Sniper!"
comments: Love + fellatio (see CCB2007) -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The coined love-and-fellatio compound and sniper image are reproduced as an intelligible English coinage.

adjudicated.jp: ペッ、と吐き捨てる。
adjudicated.en: Pah!, I spat his way.
comments: Recurring (somehow). -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The narration describes a contemptuous verbal delivery after the interjection; the English instead depicts physical spitting in another person's direction.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'I spat the words out.'

adjudicated.jp: 「けど俺の恋のライフルは、いつでも地味な君を狙って―――」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "But the Rifle of my Love always and forever aimed at plain little---"
adjudicated.assessment: The intended boast is that his love rifle is always aimed at the plain girl being addressed. The English lacks the finite verb and drops the addressee after an incomplete adjective.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'is always aimed at plain little you—'.

highlights.text: always and forever aimed at plain little

adjudicated.jp: 視線を移した瞬間、放送室の扉が閉まった。
adjudicated.en: The instant I moved my sight, the Broadcast Room door shut,
adjudicated.assessment: The source describes shifting one's gaze. 'Moved my sight' is a direct but nonidiomatic lexical transfer.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'shifted my gaze.'

adjudicated.jp: 鍵がかかる。
adjudicated.en: and the lock turned.
comments: She can disappear in the blink of Taichi's eye. Erasure of presence, in short. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The lock engaging is compactly conveyed.

adjudicated.jp: みゆきはもういない。
adjudicated.en: Miyuki is no longer among us.
comments: Lit. "not here", but given the whole theme about presences, living and more, I'll use this as a form of Pretentiously Pretentiousness that Pretentiously Pretentious etc. etc. etc. at times. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The local observation is simply that Miyuki is no longer there. The English idiom conventionally announces death and imports a grave implication absent from the line.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'Miyuki was gone.'

adjudicated.jp: 「ぬう」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Nmuh."
adjudicated.assessment: The nonlexical frustrated sound is plausibly recreated.

adjudicated.jp: 素知らぬ顔で漫画を読んでいる友貴を睨む。
adjudicated.en: I glare at Tomoki, who's reading a manga while pretending nothing happened.
adjudicated.assessment: The glare, the reading, and the feigned innocence are all preserved.

adjudicated.jp: 「その優しさがもてる秘訣ですか？」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Is that gentleness perchance the trick to becoming popular?"
comments: Formal. See CCC4012. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The pointed question about whether that kindness is the secret to popularity is accurate; the elevated diction is a voice choice rather than a factual error.

adjudicated.jp: 「はあ？」
adjudicated.en: Tomoki: "Huh?"
adjudicated.assessment: The incredulous response is accurately represented.

adjudicated.jp: 「まあいいや。それよりみゆきはどうしているの？」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Oh, forget it. More importantly, how come Miyuki's here?"
adjudicated.assessment: In context, the question naturally asks why Miyuki is present; the transition and referent remain intelligible.

adjudicated.jp: 「……おまえって後輩は平気で呼び捨てるよな」
adjudicated.en: Tomoki: "...look at you perfectly alright with calling a Kouhai without honorifics."
adjudicated.assessment: 呼び捨て means addressing someone by name without an honorific or title; it does not specifically require a surname. GHS identifies the omission but leaves kouhai untranslated and renders the observation in strained, unidiomatic English.
adjudicated.remedy: Use idiomatic English for casually calling a junior by name without a title.

highlights.text: perfectly alright with calling a Kouhai without honorifics

adjudicated.jp: 「だって後輩だよ？」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "She's a Kouhai innshe?"
adjudicated.assessment: The reply that she is a junior is retained, but the invented eye-dialect contraction is opaque and has no source basis.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'She's my junior, isn't she?'

adjudicated.jp: 静寂。
adjudicated.en: Silence.
adjudicated.assessment: The beat of silence is exactly preserved.

adjudicated.jp: 「そういうとこ尊敬するよ」
adjudicated.en: Tomoki: "I respect that part of you."
comments: See CCA0029, perhaps CCD1001B. Tomoki might sort of like Taichi that way; he certainly likes his ability to be way ruder than him. See above, the line about Character Attributes: someone is imitating here. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The stated respect for that aspect of the addressee is accurate.

adjudicated.jp: 「……福原のクラスも自習なんだってさ」
adjudicated.en: Tomoki: "...Fukuhara's class is also self-study, that's all."
adjudicated.assessment: The intended information is that Fukuhara's class also has an unsupervised study period. Equating the class itself with 'self-study' is unnatural and imprecise.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'Fukuhara's class has study hall too.'

adjudicated.jp: 「あー、なるなる」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Ahhh, got it, got it."
adjudicated.assessment: The casual realization is naturally retained.

adjudicated.jp: 謎がとけて興味も失せた。
adjudicated.en: With the enigma solved the interest vanished.
comments: Very telling this line. Taichi's someone who holds interest until it's all solved. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The narrator says that, once the mystery was solved, he also lost interest. The English substitutes a generic definite abstraction and obscures the experiencer.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'Once the mystery was solved, I lost interest.'

adjudicated.jp: 「まーた誰か弾けちゃったかな？」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Sooo I just repelled someone again, have I?"
adjudicated.assessment: The source wonders whether someone has snapped or gone off again. The English makes the speaker an agent who repelled another person, reversing the grammatical and causal structure.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'Did somebody snap again, I wonder?'

adjudicated.jp: 「……たぶんな」
adjudicated.en: Tomoki: "...mebbe."
comments: But not him. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The nonstandard eye-dialect spelling invents a marked accent not present in the neutral casual Japanese.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'Probably.'

adjudicated.jp: 椅子に座り直す。
adjudicated.en: He straightens his sitting posture.
adjudicated.assessment: The viewpoint narrator reseats himself in the chair. The translation supplies a third-person subject and changes the action into posture correction.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'I sat back down in the chair.'

adjudicated.jp: 夏の日差しは、まだ室内には入ってこない。
adjudicated.en: The sunlight of Summer doesn't yet spread throughout the room.
comments: I think this is just because of where the room is located on the building. Guessing North? I should point out that this kind of sentences are just used to glue together scene bits that don't actually flow together and look written separately, but maybe I shouldn't unravel this thing TOO far. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The sunlight has not yet entered the room at all; 'doesn't spread throughout' permits partial entry and changes the spatial state.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'The summer sunlight hadn't reached the room yet.'

adjudicated.jp: 「放送部はいいよなぁ。この部屋が使えるだけでいい」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "The Broadcast Club is sooo nice. Nice even just 'cause we can use this room."
adjudicated.assessment: The appreciation of the club based solely on access to the room is conveyed, with deliberate repetition matching the casual enthusiasm.

adjudicated.jp: 「そうだね」
adjudicated.en: Tomoki: "Ain't that right."
adjudicated.assessment: The source is a low-energy affirmation, 'Yeah' or 'That's true.' The English recasts it as a tag-like demand for agreement and adds marked dialect.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'Yeah.'

adjudicated.jp: 読書中の友貴は返事も気怠い。
adjudicated.en: Even Tomoki's replies are listless when he's reading.
comments: Just like Taichi's when he's in his delusional mode. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The listless quality of the reader's response is accurately described.

adjudicated.jp: 「……なに読んでるの？」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "...what'cha reading there?"
adjudicated.assessment: The casual question about the reading material is accurately conveyed.

adjudicated.jp: 「サイコマン」
adjudicated.en: Tomoki: "Psychoman."
comments: Although a guy named Saikoman seems to be the villain in an old one-shot anime movie in-author crossover between Ninja Hattori-kun and Perman called ESP Wars http://anidb.net/perl-bin/animedb.pl?show=anime&aid=4742 that's very much insufficient to call it a reference. Far more likely it's just about the Saiko multiple meaning from CCA0001 (and more importantly CCA0030). Might be something of a Ultraman/Superman reference, too? -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The title is directly and consistently romanized.

adjudicated.jp: 「八束が死んで、真犯人は真崎だと判明した」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Yatsuka dies, the true culprit is proven to be Masaki."
comments: http://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E5%85%AB%E6%9D%9F%E7%94%BA <- hmmm. But this thing is about epic-level meta. Eight-bundle, the bundle of eights dies; the culprit is pure/true-Saki, same Saki as Tasaki. The Bundle of Eights (there's waaay lots) is killed by Tasaki when True, and the True Tasaki would be the Christian Tasaki. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The reported revelation is substantially correct, but 'the culprit is proven to be' is an unidiomatic passive construction for a discovery within a narrative.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'and Masaki turned out to be the real culprit.'

adjudicated.jp: 「言うなよーっ！！」
adjudicated.en: Tomoki: "Don't spoil iiit!!!"
adjudicated.assessment: The shouted demand not to reveal the plot is accurately conveyed.

adjudicated.jp: 「やるかーっ！」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Wooon't I!"
adjudicated.assessment: In the exchange, the emphatic declaration that he will do it is functionally preserved.

adjudicated.jp: 「もう言うなよっ、魔獣列島のオチとか絶対言うなよ！」
adjudicated.en: Tomoki: "Don'tcha spoil the rest! And absolutely not the ending of the Islands of the Demons!"
comments: No references I can source. Demon-beast archipelago/chain of islands = Japan under the domain of Satan. Certainly Japan is the most famous example of the word 列島, and it's basic Christian theology. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The escalating prohibition against further spoilers, especially the named work's ending, is retained.

adjudicated.jp: 「アンデルセン神父が味方のスパイでさらわれた依子を助けてくれた！」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Father Anderson rescues the kidnapped Yoriko with help from a friendly spy."
comments: Father Anderson -> http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hellsing Began 1997, as with this scene. But I suspect that's just plausible deniability: the end of Japan, the land under the domain of Satan, is that a Christian priest, with assistance from a local (coughTanakacough), rescues the "dependent child" AKA mankind, see all the stuff about Alter Egos etc. for what is meant about "dependence". It only sounds like projecting without knowing that Cross Channel is a fundamentally Christian tale, then it's so blatantly obvious that you can see Tanaka giggling mad as he writes this, certain no one in the world would ever get it. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The source identifies Father Andersen himself as an allied spy who rescues the abducted person. The English invents a separate friendly spy who assists him.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'Father Andersen was an allied spy, and he rescued the kidnapped Yoriko.'

highlights.text: with help from a friendly spy

adjudicated.jp: 「言うなよっ」
adjudicated.en: Tomoki: "Don't spoil it!"
adjudicated.assessment: The renewed demand not to say it is correctly localized as a spoiler warning.

adjudicated.jp: 「言論統制反対！」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Regulation of free speech ostracized!"
comments: This sort of spoils a later gag :-( -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The line is a slogan opposing censorship or speech control. 'Ostracized' neither expresses opposition nor forms an idiomatic English slogan.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'Down with censorship!'

adjudicated.jp: 「裏切りものーっ！」
adjudicated.en: Tomoki: "Traitor!"
comments: His mouth calls him a traitor, but his actions don't put Taichi on the same level as his sister. Hypocrite. -GHS
SEF 101 0
HACK independent CG shake -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The shouted accusation of betrayal is exact.

adjudicated.jp: 「エピクロス主義者っ！」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Epicurean!"
comments: This sounds like a dumb overwrought insult, until considering the above as well as later: according to Wiki, "Epicurus['s] materialism led him to a general attack on superstition and divine intervention." See CCD1001B for when TEH MIRACL3S lol cures his feet. Truly, no insult worse than this for Tomoki. -GHS
SEF 101 0
HACK independent CG shake -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The mock-philosophical insult is directly preserved.

adjudicated.jp: もみあいに。
adjudicated.en: Push, shove, jostle and struggle.
comments: Though "a meeting of rubs" is sorta funny in its own way, straight isn't evocative enough. Wait, something involving Taichi and Tomoki being straight is not evoca-GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The transition into a physical scuffle is expanded but accurately conveyed.

adjudicated.jp: 中扉が開いて、顔を出したみゆきが小さく叫んだ。
adjudicated.en: The inner door opens, and from Miyuki's peeking face comes a whispered shout.
adjudicated.assessment: She gives a small or quiet cry after peeking out. 'Whispered shout' is internally contradictory and turns a restrained exclamation into an impossible manner of shouting.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'called out softly.'

adjudicated.jp: 「先輩！　先生が来た！」
adjudicated.en: Miyuki: "Senpai! Teacher's coming!"
comments: Now this is interesting: shouldn't the Broadcast Room be sealed? How does she see Mammoth coming, and most importantly, how come hiding inside the room prevent Mammoth from seeing them? ...is she just breaking them up by faking this, and Taichi is playing along due to Shimura Phenomenon (i.e. he was told it's true therefore it is)? Now on this I have no answer. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The urgent warning that a teacher has arrived or is approaching is functionally accurate.

adjudicated.jp: 「えっ！」
adjudicated.en: Tomoki: "Eh?!"
adjudicated.assessment: The startled reaction is preserved.

adjudicated.jp: 「あれ……太一？」
adjudicated.en: Tomoki: "Wha-... Taichi?"
adjudicated.assessment: The confused recognition and name are accurately conveyed.

adjudicated.jp: 馬鹿だな、隠れが遅い。
adjudicated.en: Fool, you're slow to hide.
comments: He can already kill his presence. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The contemptuous judgment that the other person was too slow to hide is retained.

adjudicated.jp: 俺はもう廊下側から死角になる位置に身を潜め終えた。
adjudicated.en: I was already done concealing myself in a spot blind from the corridor side.
adjudicated.assessment: The narrator has hidden in a position outside the corridor's line of sight. The English renders the Japanese spatial relation as an unidiomatic 'spot blind from' construction.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'a spot that couldn't be seen from the corridor.'

highlights.text: a spot blind from the corridor side

adjudicated.jp: 友貴はおたおたと右往左往している。
adjudicated.en: Tomoki is flapping about right and left in confusion.
adjudicated.assessment: The character is panicking and running or looking helplessly this way and that. 'Flapping' suggests wings or loose material and does not idiomatically describe the action.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'Tomoki darted helplessly back and forth.'

adjudicated.jp: 「先輩こっちこっち！」
adjudicated.en: Miyuki: "Senpai, here, here!"
adjudicated.assessment: The urgent summons toward the speaker is accurately retained.

adjudicated.jp: 身を低くして、友貴は放送室に逃げた。
adjudicated.en: Lowering his posture, Tomoki escapes into the Broadcast Room,
adjudicated.assessment: The source depicts crouching or keeping low while fleeing. 'Lowering his posture' is a literal but nonidiomatic rendering of bodily movement.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'Keeping low, Tomoki fled into the broadcast room.'

adjudicated.jp: みゆきと一緒に。
adjudicated.en: together with Miyuki.
adjudicated.assessment: The companion fragment is accurately carried over.

adjudicated.jp: あ、そっちのが良かった……。
adjudicated.en: Ah, I wish I'd done that...
adjudicated.assessment: The immediate regret at not choosing the other option is naturally conveyed.

adjudicated.jp: くそ、こんなことくらいで泣くな俺っ。
adjudicated.en: Crap, don't you dare cry over something like this, me!
adjudicated.assessment: The comic self-directed command not to cry over something so minor is preserved, including its marked self-address.

adjudicated.jp: 扉が締まると同時に、廊下を身長１９０センチの筋肉が通りかかった。
adjudicated.en: Simultaneously with the closing of that door, 190cm of muscle happened to pass by in the corridor.
comments: Remember that this is Japan, where the Giant Schoolgirl archetype barely touches 170cm. Machiko was just defined as tall for being 173. Hmmn, 10 surely, but 9-1 is, uhm, hmmm, erm, where's the calculator... 3. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The timing is correct, but the nominalized construction is an unnatural calque where English requires a finite temporal clause.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'Just as the door closed,'

highlights.text: Simultaneously with the closing of that door

adjudicated.jp: マンモスだ。
adjudicated.en: It's Mammoth.
adjudicated.assessment: The nickname identification is exact.

adjudicated.jp: 見つかったらただではすまない。
adjudicated.en: If he finds me, this won't just go away.
adjudicated.assessment: The source says that being discovered will mean not getting off lightly. The English instead suggests that an abstract situation will persist, losing the threat of consequences to the speaker.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'If he catches me, I won't get off easy.'

adjudicated.jp: 以前、奴がスチール缶を片手でピンポン玉ほどのサイズに握りつぶす瞬間を見たことがある。
adjudicated.en:
Once, I saw this guy instantly crush a steel can
to the size of a ping-pong ball with one hand.
comments: This is utterly ludicrous, of course. Who IS this person in reality? -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The remembered feat, object, hand, and resulting size are all accurately conveyed.

adjudicated.jp: しかもやつの体罰は、２１世紀に適応していて侮れない。
adjudicated.en:
And this guy's corporal punishment is formidably
conforming to the 21st Century.
comments: Still doesn't contradict it being 1997. Same Conformity as the Coefficient, interestingly enough. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The source says his corporal punishment has adapted to the twenty-first century and is not to be underestimated. 'Formidably conforming' is not idiomatic and conflates adaptation with obedience to a standard.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'His corporal punishment has adapted to the twenty-first century, too, so it can't be taken lightly.'

adjudicated.jp: 痕跡を残さず苦痛を与える術に長けているのだ。
adjudicated.en:
He is excellent in the art of inflicting agony
without leaving any visible trace.
comments: The original text had a minor typo. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The skill at inflicting pain without leaving marks is accurately conveyed.

adjudicated.jp: これで某婦人告訴団体ペタも恐くないって寸法さ！
adjudicated.en:
And with these measures he has nothing to fear
from that 『Women's Lawsuit Organization * PTA』!
comments: http://www6.ocn.ne.jp/~rejina/cc/motoneta.html the PTA in Japan seems to be at the forefront of this kind of stuff, and it'll be even more obvious that this is the reference in CCB2009 when the PTA starts censoring Taichi's porn via Modern Tsundere archetype Touko. (There's a sentence I didn't expect to type in my life.) -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The substitution of PTA for the source parody name Peta is a documented attempt to make the censorship-group reference legible in English. The raw annotation marker is poor presentation and the exact name is lost, but this is a debatable localization choice rather than an unsupported mistranslation.
adjudicated.remedy: Preserve the parody name cleanly while making its institutional target intelligible.

adjudicated.jp: マンモスはそれはもうピグミーマーモセット並に、恐ろしく狡猾な苦しみマッスルなのである。
adjudicated.en:
Assuredly, Mammoth has terrifyingly crafty
agony muscles on the level of pygmy marmosets.
comments: http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pygmy_marmoset they... are not threating at all. Supposing his "agony muscles" are metaphorical? This seems over the top dumb even for Taichi. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The source is itself a deliberately absurd pileup, and the English retains Mammoth, pygmy marmosets, terrifying craftiness, suffering, and the closing muscle coinage. Its attachment is hard to parse, but the material and comic overload are substantially present.
adjudicated.remedy: Clarify which comparison modifies Mammoth while preserving the absurd muscle coinage.

adjudicated.jp: 巨体がのしのしと通り過ぎていく。
adjudicated.en: His musculature goes lumbering past.
adjudicated.assessment: The huge muscular body lumbering past is vividly and accurately represented through metonymy.

adjudicated.jp: 途中、視線を室内に向けた。
adjudicated.en: Midway, his sight turns inside the room,
adjudicated.assessment: The person turns his gaze into the room. Making 'sight' itself turn and using 'inside' as its destination is an unidiomatic transfer of the Japanese construction.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'On the way past, he looked into the room.'

highlights.text: his sight turns inside the room

adjudicated.en: Shigezo: "..."
adjudicated.assessment: The silent pause is preserved.

adjudicated.jp: そのまま立ち去る。
adjudicated.en: and with that he leaves.
adjudicated.assessment: The departure without further action is accurately conveyed.

adjudicated.jp: 原始人に狩られてしまえ、と呪っておく。
adjudicated.en: Go get hunted down by a caveman!, I curse him.
adjudicated.assessment: The curse's content is present, but the English joins a malformed imperative, exclamation point, comma, and reporting clause into an ungrammatical sentence.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'May a caveman hunt you down, I cursed him.'

highlights.text: Go get hunted down by a caveman!, I curse him.

adjudicated.jp: 「シベリアの凍土こそ、おまえにふさわしいグレイヴヤードになるだろう」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "The Siberian tundra would make a fitting graveyard for the likes of you!"
comments: Let's start with some katakana weirdness then. Gureivuya-do is a much less popular spelling than gureibuya-do. Not that it matters, since he should've used "grave". -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The theatrical condemnation to a Siberian tundra graveyard is accurately and naturally retained.

adjudicated.jp: 身を出す。
adjudicated.en: I show myself.
adjudicated.assessment: Emerging from concealment is acceptably conveyed as showing oneself.

adjudicated.jp: 「あぶないあぶない」
adjudicated.en: Tomoki: "Close so close!"
adjudicated.assessment: Close so close is readily intelligible as a telegraphic relieved exclamation. Missing punctuation is an optional copyedit, not a confirmed source-bound error.
adjudicated.remedy: Optional idiomatic revision; no confirmed source-bound correction is established.

adjudicated.jp: 「カーテンつけた方がいいですよねぇ、廊下側の窓」
adjudicated.en: Miyuki: "We should just put up curtains on that corridor window."
adjudicated.assessment: The suggestion to install curtains on the corridor-side window is accurately conveyed.

adjudicated.jp: 「禁止されてるんだよ。学校もよくわかってるよな」
adjudicated.en: Tomoki: "That was forbidden. School got wise to that already."
comments: They don't forbid them to have obviously non-club non-school related stuff in there, obvious pictures in front of the window nooo problem, but curtains? Nope, that's the line! Setting aside how they can easily be heard inside of there. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The source says the curtains are currently prohibited. The past tense implies the prohibition no longer applies and shifts the practical reason they cannot install them.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'That's forbidden.'

adjudicated.jp: 「いい手がある」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "There's something we could do."
adjudicated.assessment: The announcement of a good plan is naturally paraphrased.

adjudicated.en: Miyuki: "..."
adjudicated.assessment: The silent response is preserved.

adjudicated.en: Tomoki: "..."
adjudicated.assessment: The second silent response is preserved; adjacent canonical addresses uniquely bind this otherwise duplicated text to the cited occurrence.

adjudicated.jp: 「あー、諸君らが俺をどう思っているかは知っている。だがこれはつまらないギャグではなくマジでいい手なのだ」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Ahhh, I know what you ladies think of me. But this isn't some annoying gag, I really think there's something we could do."
comments: He totally means to refer them both as 'ladies'. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The collective address means 'you people' or 'all of you' and includes the group present. The English changes it to a gendered address unsupported by the wording and local participants.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'I know what you all think of me.'

adjudicated.jp: 「どんなんです？」
adjudicated.en: Miyuki: "What would that be?"
adjudicated.assessment: The request to explain the proposed plan is naturally conveyed.

adjudicated.jp: 「友貴、マシン使えるようにしてくれよ。あとデジカメ」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Tomoki, get me the machine back in working order. Also, the digital camera."
comments: This is a somewhat modern thing to have in 1998, but this is Gunjou; all the stuff here is high tech for the time. Miki will use a disposable camera with film, tying in to how the Club not having LCDs - but Youko having them - is significant. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: Both requests—to make the machine usable and provide the digital camera—are accurately retained.

adjudicated.jp: 「はーん？」
adjudicated.en: Tomoki: "Huuuh?"
adjudicated.assessment: The drawn-out skeptical reaction is effectively represented.

withheld.jp: 身長１７３センチの長身でグラマラスなダイナマイト・ボディの持ち主でしかも美形でパリッとしていてブランドものの縁なし眼鏡が似合っていて濃紺の光沢を持ったロングヘアをしゃれっ気たっぷりにアップにしているばかりか艶めかしくつやめく肉厚の唇が魅惑的な、俺的最強生命体の一人である。
withheld.en:
Beguiling not just by being the possessor of
a Glamorous Dynamite Body of the impressive
height of 173cm that is nevertheless
beautifully shaped as well as being posh with
those brand-name rimless glasses that so suit her
and her long hair with its dark blue highlights
that in ample fashion-consciousness she keeps in
